record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r. Theorem 1.21 constructs a trace φ_{r,\infty}(·|A) on A^{APP}_{r,\infty}. Determine whether this trace is spectral, meaning that for each operator in the ideal its value can be reconstructed from the operator's eigenvalue sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between (arbitrary) Banach spaces, and let $\mathfrak{A}$ be a quasi-Banach operator ideal, i.e. a subclass $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak{A}}$ making each component $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ a quasi-Banach space and satisfying the usual ideal property $\|BTA\|_{\mathfrak{A}}\le \|B\|\,\|T\|_{\mathfrak{A}}\,\|A\|$.

For an operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ define the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|: F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}\,F<n\},\qquad n=1,2,\dots$$
For $0<r<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type approximation ideal
$$\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}=\{T\in\mathcal{L}: \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} a_n(T)<\infty\}.$$

Say that a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is of exact trace type $1/r$ (with $0<r<\infty$) in the sense required for the construction of the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$: there exists a continuous trace on $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ obtained by an averaging/limit procedure applied to the approximation numbers and the trace structure on finite-rank operators of $\mathfrak{A}$, yielding a linear functional
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})\colon\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}\to\mathbb{C}$$
that vanishes on commutators $ST-TS$ whenever both $S,T$ make sense in the ideal.

A trace $\varphi$ on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{I}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ is called spectral if its value on every $T\in\mathfrak{I}$ depends only on the eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(T))$ of $T$ (counted with algebraic multiplicities and arranged so that $|\lambda_1(T)|\ge|\lambda_2(T)|\ge\cdots$); equivalently, there exists a symmetric functional $\Lambda$ on the corresponding space of eigenvalue sequences such that $\varphi(T)=\Lambda(\lambda_n(T))$ for every $T\in\mathfrak{I}$.

Problem. For every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ of exact trace type $1/r$, decide whether the trace
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$$
on $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is spectral.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem about whether a specific trace constructed on the approximation Lorentz-type ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is spectral. While there are general results characterizing spectral traces on Hilbert-space operator ideals (e.g. Sukochev–Zanin "Which traces are spectral?"), no resolution of the spectrality of $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$ for general Banach operator ideals of exact trace type $1/r$ was located.

status_evidence.title: Which traces are spectral?
status_evidence.snippet: A positive trace on an arbitrary ideal is spectral if and only if it is monotone with respect to logarithmic submajorization.
status_evidence.claim: Spectrality of traces is characterized in the Hilbert space / semifinite von Neumann setting, but not in the general Banach-space ideal setting at issue here.

status_evidence.title: Modern Applications of s-numbers and Operator Ideals (Oberwolfach Report)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces and outstanding problems posed by Pietsch.
status_evidence.claim: Spectrality questions for traces constructed via approximation-number Lorentz ideals on general Banach spaces remain among the listed open problems.
